transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands — Jan 27 2026 | 16:00 PST | Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Ava, Diego, Maya, Samir, Eleanor, Liam, Priya + company-wide attendees (virtual)

00:00 Ava Chen: Okay hey everyone hello, thanks for joining the January all-hands. I know some folks are joining from EMEA and APAC so appreciate the weird hours, um we'll keep to about 45-60 minutes and then open Q&A.
00:12 Diego Martinez: Quick note on audio — we're recording and transcript's on the event page.
00:20 Ava Chen: Alright first slide, business update. Revenue is up 18% q/q, usage growth in Hosted API continues but the big lifts are coming from Dedicated renewals. We closed three new Dedicated contracts last month, one global SaaS and one fintech with very strict SSO/KMS requirements.
00:45 Maya Patel: To add, churn is down, but we still have pockets where onboarding time is long — particularly Private deployments where network config or our KMS integrations take extra cycles.
01:05 Priya Singh: We're pairing SEs with AE for the top 10 accounts to speed that up, it's already moved two deals forward.
01:20 Ava Chen: Good, good. Diego, can you take us through the reliability metrics?
01:24 Diego Martinez: Sure, overall p99 latency is stable but we had a brief outage on Jan 14th where a kernel selection regression caused increased tail latency for some longer sequences. Post-mortem's in Confluence (link in chat). Root cause was a bad fallback path when quantized kernels hit an edge case — we shipped a fix within 3 hours and a mitigation in 30 minutes.
01:55 Samir Rao: We're also rolling out the new canary routing rules so that when we detect kernel mismatch we fall back to a compatible variant before customer-facing latency increases. Need to tighten the monitoring alert thresholds.
02:12 Diego Martinez: Yeah, and small note — transcription engine said 'kernel' as 'colonel' in a few places, sorry transcript folks.
02:20 Audience Question (Slack): Any change to pricing for Dedicated or Reserved?
02:25 Ava Chen: No immediate pricing changes, but Optimize will launch new recommendations that should reduce unit cost for many customers; we'll share benchmarks next week.
02:35 Eleanor Park: On product roadmap, three highlights: 1) Dedicated autoscaling GA — expected in Q1 end, 2) Private deployment GA checklist and enterprise onboarding improvements, 3) Redwood Optimize v2 (better quantization recommendations and batch suggestions). We demoed the autoscaler internally last week and saw 25% improvement in utilization for mixed workloads.
03:10 Samir Rao: For the autoscaler, note that burst capacity still needs a policy for latency SLOs, so we'll expose a per-pool policy flag.
03:25 Liam O'Neal: DX improvements — new quickstarts for Java and Go are landing Feb 2, plus streaming SDK examples and a quick opentelemetry tracing snippet.
03:40 Ava Chen: Nice. Hiring update? Maya?
03:44 Maya Patel: We're ramping infra hires, two senior infra engineers, one performance engineer, and three DX engineers. Samir will own the infrastructure hiring schedule.
04:00 Samir Rao: Yep, I'll share a 30/60/90 with hires, interviews pipeline, and where we need help.
04:12 Priya Singh: Sales update — closed logos include Acme Health (Private pilot), FinSched (Dedicated), and a strategic partnership with a cloud reseller in APAC. We also have 8 RFPs in progress.
04:35 Audience (Voice): Congrats on the wins — quick question about SOC2 and ISO readiness from a customer perspective?
04:42 Maya Patel: We're on track for SOC 2 Type II for our control plane and have started evidence collection for the Private package; ISO 27001 planning is next quarter. There's a security packet in the shared drive.
05:05 Diego Martinez: Also, for customers asking about data residency, our Private deployment templates now include region-specific KMS hooks and audit log export options.
05:25 Ava Chen: Thank you. Quick customer story — enterprise X (redacted) moved from self-hosting to Redwood Dedicated because the unit economics were better once we accounted for ops overhead. They cited our routing/fallback story as key.
05:45 Audience (Chat): Any update on model catalog and open models?
05:50 Eleanor Park: We're expanding our catalog with two community open models tuned for inference speed; we'll mark them Redwood-verified and include performance profiles in the catalog page. Expect that next month.
06:10 Diego Martinez: Small technical deep-dive later this week for anyone interested in kernel selection and quantization artifacts — SEs, please join.
06:20 Audience Question: What's the plan for on-prem air-gapped?
06:25 Maya Patel: We're on track for an air-gapped on-prem package, the blocker is automating license and updates. We're aiming for a beta in Q2.
06:40 Ava Chen: Ok leadership changes — we're creating a new role, Head of Platform Partnerships to focus on channel and reseller plays, hiring lead to be posted next week.
06:55 Priya Singh: That role will help with marketplace listings and compliance partners in EU and APAC.
07:10 Ava Chen: Alright we'll open for Q&A. Reminder: post-mortem and runbook link in chat, GA checklist link in product channel.
07:20 Audience Q&A highlights:
07:21 Employee A: Can we get a walkthrough of the Private onboarding checklist?
07:24 Eleanor Park: Yes, I'll schedule a 30-min demo session and share the checklist.
07:30 Employee B: Will we proactively notify customers about the kernel regression?
07:33 Diego Martinez: We did a targeted customer notification for impacted customers and will schedule a summary for CSMs to share broadly.
07:45 Employee C (muffled): Any changes to quarterly OKRs?
07:48 Ava Chen: Minor tweaks — I'll share revised OKRs after leadership sync.
08:00 Closing: Thanks everyone, please fill out the feedback form. Links: Post-mortem: https://confluence.redwood.internal/postmortem/2026-01-14-kernel-regression | GA checklist: https://docs.redwood.internal/private-ga-checklist | Deck: https://drive.redwood.internal/allhands/jan-2026-deck.pdf
08:18 End of recording

Notes on transcript: Minor transcription errors (names, acronyms) present; speaker labels are best-effort. The meeting included a short live poll (results in chat) and multiple breakout follow-ups scheduled.
